subject: reasoning
question: A two-digit number is 5 times the sum of its digits. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 9 more than the original. What is the number?
solution:
Let the two-digit number be 10a + b, where

 
• a = tens digit
 
• b = units digit

 

The number is 5 times the sum of its digits:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25c15c89539ec739fd1b60b611809c0012b9858b704a1777cc5a5b35850f68a6.png] **
 

Expand:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea155b67d45b76a4cd9f4021767357c8b9f3650a26291d4e664b3ec418bd3905.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c6685326de273a0d2e4f2b2abd4d840530729c5e58291f9db389eb17084e771.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/617347584c3c7018a193a9ca8e8706551d24f9d7b0a6e4bb6adb2e0d34f1ba80.png] 

 

So b must be a multiple of 5.

Let [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b8d3f91f7a66d4a4e832731fb4fa18d0bc330d2d7c6d0afe7d0d3816238df97c.png] , then [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa8b96e13a9da98aea4fc5fe66d20e918df88ce2ea0f3eea88962bea8fd35b84.png] .

Since a and b are digits (1–9), only **k = 1** works.

So:

 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3bf0191dd999ce2ea44ec37d9c6aacc74d13ee1f9463e2e1fb7c6e229ee4057e.png] 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96615da61800b1d19ca5064e19ce435f65e13ddfb656482cb5112896685b33b2.png] 

Number = **45**

Reversing digits gives a number **9 more**:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f878604bd5ce7045349a2e7331cb4a7c8e538c19ca367b262442e876840ba05.png] 

 

Check with 45:

Reversed = 54

54 = 45 + 9

**The number is 45.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"**
